transcript.text:
To help narrow this down, I need to know exactly what happens when you try to use it. Does the machine have absolutely no power (no lights or sounds), or does it start but then stop? Also, please check that the door is clicking shut firmly, as many dryers will not run if they think the door is open.
[Helpful to see: image "Tumble dryer runs but doesn't heat — what to check" — If the drum turns but the clothes stay wet, it's usually a heating fault — and the most common cause is restricted airflow, which you can fix yourself. Clean the fluff filter and the condenser and clear the vents/ducts. Switch the dryer off and let it cool first.]
Lights come on but nothing happens when I press start, no sound. The door doesn't click shut, it swings back slightly open.

[Heading: Door catch or handle fault preventing latch]
The fact that the door swings back open means the dryer's safety interlock (which prevents it from running if the door is open) will never trigger. The machine won't start because it thinks the door isn't shut. This points to a mechanical issue with the door catch or handle rather than an electrical fault. Please unplug the dryer, then check the plastic catch on the edge of the door and the slot in the frame. If you see fluff blocking it, clear it. If the plastic is cracked or broken, that part needs replacing. Let me know what you find with the catch.
Found it - the plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, I found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

[Heading: Broken door handle/catch mechanism]
That confirms the issue: the plastic catch on your door has snapped off. You need to replace the door handle assembly (often called the door catch or latch). This is a standard owner-replaceable part for most tumble dryers. You will need your model number to find the correct part; check the rating plate inside the door frame or on the back of the machine. Once you have the new part, fit it according to the instructions (usually just unclipping the old one and snapping the new one into place), then test the door again to ensure it clicks shut firmly before running a cycle.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I don't know the model number offhand. I'll have a look inside the door and let you know.

That sounds like the right place to look. The model number is usually on a sticker inside the door frame or on the back of the machine. Once you have it, please share both the brand and the full model code so I can confirm exactly which replacement part fits your dryer.
ok, the dryer is a Hotpoint. I'm going to look inside the door for the model number now.

To ensure I give you the correct replacement part, please share the exact model number once you've found it (usually on a silver or white sticker inside the door frame or on the rear of the machine). Once I have that, I can confirm the specific handle assembly you need.
I haven't found it yet, still looking. Is there anything else I should check on the door while I'm at it?

However, please do check if the door hangs straight or sags slightly, as this can affect how well a new catch works. Also, look at the hinges where the door attaches to the cabinet—are they loose or cracked? If you find any major damage there, let me know, but otherwise just keep looking for that model number sticker inside the door frame or on the back.
Door hangs straight, I think. Hinges look fine, nothing loose or cracked. Still can't see the model number yet.

[Heading: Broken door handle/catch assembly]
You need to replace the entire door handle assembly (often called the latch or catch) for your Hotpoint tumble dryer. To find the correct part, please keep looking for the model number sticker inside the door frame or on the back of the machine. Once you have the full model code, share it here and I can confirm exactly which replacement part fits your specific dryer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Found it, the sticker was inside the door recess. I can't make it out properly though, what should I do next?

Since the door catch is broken and you need to replace it, getting the exact model number is critical because Hotpoint makes many different dryer models that look similar but use different parts. Once I have that, I can confirm exactly which handle assembly fits your machine.
